scope: Targeted primary-method follow-up motivated by the observed option-label/position pattern; not a second daily crawl or a claim that all papers were newly published today.

works.title: Large Language Models Are Not Robust Multiple Choice Selectors
works.authors: Chujie Zheng; Hao Zhou; Fandong Meng; Jie Zhou; Minlie Huang
works.version_link: One work, preprint and conference version not double-counted
works.read: v4 experimental setup and sections2.4-3.1; earlier v3 sections3.1-3.3 also inspected
works.method: Separates option-ID token bias from displayed position through ID shuffling/removal; evaluates probability-based selection and proposes prior-estimation calibration with a permutation baseline.
works.decision: Do not call label preference, option permutations or generic calibration a new algorithm. Our current A/first-position binding cannot identify these two causes separately; no logits/PriDe implementation was evaluated.
works.access_issue: Direct OpenReview PDF returned a browser-verification challenge; used official proceedings and author arXiv full text instead.

works.title: Lost in the Prompt Order: Revealing the Limitations of Causal Attention in Language Models
works.version_link: Matching title/authors and arXiv venue note; count as one work
works.read: Formal PDF sections2-4 including architecture comparison, option recall, context removal, attention interventions and differing scoring modes
works.method: Studies context/question/option ordering, comparing architectures and interventions rather than assuming one cause from an observed contrast.
works.decision: Our context already precedes the options, so their context-after-options account is not a direct explanation. Prompt rearrangement or option repetition alone is not an originality claim, nor did we reproduce their internal-mechanism evidence.

algorithm_status: No new algorithm. Existing prior art strengthens the decision not to pursue a generic MCQ debiasing detour as PersonaSLM novelty.
daily_monitor_boundary: Existing arXiv/Crossref/OpenAlex metadata task already ran today and was not restarted. Known direct daily ACL/OpenReview/SemanticScholar coverage gaps remain; targeted primary reading is not a scheduled all-source deep-analysis service.
